summary.short: Singapore's general data protection statute. It governs organisations' collection, use and disclosure of personal data (consent, purpose, access, protection, retention, cross-border transfer, breach notification), creates the Do Not Call Registry, and provides for Commission directions, financial penalties and private action. Commenced in phases from 2 January 2013.
summary.long: The Act governs collection, use and disclosure of personal data by organisations, balancing individuals' right to protect their data with organisations' need to use it for appropriate purposes. Parts 3 to 6B bind organisations, not individuals acting personally or domestically, employees acting in employment, or public agencies; records at least 100 years old are outside the Act. Parts 2 and 3 establish the Personal Data Protection Commission and accountability duties. Part 4 covers consent, deemed consent, withdrawal, collection without consent and purpose limitation. Parts 5 and 6 cover access, correction, accuracy, protection, retention and transfers outside Singapore. Part 6A requires breach assessment and notification. Part 9 creates the Do Not Call Registry; Part 9A prohibits dictionary attacks and address-harvesting software; Part 9B creates offences for unauthorised disclosure, improper use and re-identification of anonymised information. Part 9C provides directions, financial penalties, voluntary undertakings and a right of private action; Part 9D provides appeals. Part 10 covers guidelines, investigation powers, offences and penalties, employer liability and regulations. Only Part 1 and the outline are reproduced in the supplied text; penalty amounts and the operative wording of later Parts are absent.

“personal data” means data, whether true or not, about an individual who can be identified
“individual” means a natural person, whether living or deceased
“organisation” includes any individual, company, association or body of persons, corporate or unincorporated
“data intermediary” means an organisation which processes personal data on behalf of another organisation but does not include an employee of that other organisation
“processing”, in relation to personal data, means the carrying out of any operation or set of operations in relation to the personal data
the Government, including any ministry, department, agency, or organ of State
does not include an individual acting in his or her personal or domestic capacity
“employee” includes a volunteer
an individual’s name, position name or title, business telephone number, business address, business electronic mail address or business fax number
“publicly available”, in relation to personal data about an individual, means personal data that is generally available to the public
means personal data about an individual that is derived by an organisation in the course of business from other personal data

“user activity data”, in relation to an organisation, means personal data about an individual that is created in the course or as a result of the individual’s use of any product or service provided by the organisation
means personal data provided by an individual to the organisation

obligations.summary: An organisation carries the same obligations under the Act for personal data processed on its behalf and for its purposes by a data intermediary as if it had processed the data itself (Section 4(3)). Applies to Parts 3 to 6A as provided in Section 4(1) and (2).
obligations.applies_from: 2 January 2013 (Part 1 commencement per the legislative history note)
obligations.conditional_on: personal data processed on the organisation's behalf and for its purposes by a data intermediary

evidence.quote: An organisation has the same obligation under this Act in respect of personal data processed on its behalf and for its purposes by a data intermediary as if the personal data were processed by the organisation itself.

obligations.summary: The Minister may, by notification in the Gazette, specify statutory bodies established under a public Act for a public function as public agencies for the purposes of the Act.
obligations.applies_from: 2 January 2013 (Part 1 commencement per the legislative history note)

evidence.quote: The Minister may, by notification in the Gazette, specify any statutory body established under a public Act for a public function to be a public agency for the purposes of this Act.
